- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast mid-range by 2–5% to capture mean reversion bias.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment swings >0.3 in last 5 days.  
- When sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often ignores sentiment and forecasts downward — if sentiment >0.3 and price is trending down, add 1–2% upward adjustment to reflect sentiment-driven reversal.  
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends — if last 3 sentiment values are negative, add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to forecast to counteract lagged sell-off.
